title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Purpose
-------
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response process. It consolidates incident lifecycle steps, runbook templates for common failures, postmortem expectations, on-call rotation rules, game day guidance, and customer status/communication templates. The goal is to ensure incidents are handled consistently, quickly, and with clear ownership so we meet our SLOs and improve system reliability over time.

Scope
-----
Applies to all production-facing services managed by Redwood (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, private deployment control plane). This document covers: detection & alerting, triage, mitigation, escalations, postmortem process, runbook patterns, on-call scheduling, and public/customer comms.

Key contacts and channels
-------------------------
- Primary on-call Slack channel: #oncall-incidents
- Incident commander (IC) temporary channel pattern: #incident-<INCIDENT-ID> (create on incident start)
- PagerDuty service: Redwood-Prod (see PagerDuty escalation policy)
- PagerDuty escalation: primary -> secondary (15m) -> engineering manager (30m) -> SRE lead (60m)
- Status page: status.redwood.ai
- Postmortem repo: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems

Incident severity and SLO mapping
--------------------------------
We use four severity levels. Severity guides escalation, communications, and postmortem requirements.

1) Sev 1 (SEV-1) — Critical outage
   - Definition: System-wide outage or severe degradation that blocks customer requests or causes API failures and violates high-priority SLOs (e.g., API availability < 99.9% in 15m window).
   - Triage target: 0-5 minutes.
   - PagerDuty: immediate page to primary and secondary.
   - Postmortem: required within 72 hours (initial draft).

2) Sev 2 — Major degradation
   - Definition: Significant feature degradation for many customers (e.g., sustained latency > 2x p50/p95 targets, substantial throughput reduction).
   - Triage target: 5-15 minutes.
   - PagerDuty: page primary.
   - Postmortem: required within 7 days.

3) Sev 3 — Partial loss or isolated customer impact
   - Definition: Impact limited to subset of customers or features, workarounds exist.
   - Triage target: 1 hour.
   - Postmortem: discretionary; recommend write-up for recurring issues.

4) Sev 4 — Informational / maintenance
   - Definition: Planned maintenance, non-urgent degradations, or cosmetic issues.

Roles & responsibilities
------------------------
- First responder: Acknowledge alert, run initial triage checklist, and escalate if needed.
- Incident Commander (IC): Owns coordination, communications, and decision-making until incident is resolved.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Service owners, database/network/infra owners who perform remediation work.
- Communications lead: Publishes updates to internal channels and status page; coordinates customer messaging.
- Postmortem author: Writes the postmortem and coordinates reviews.

On-call rotations and handoffs
-----------------------------
- Rotation model: Primary on-call rotates weekly; secondary rotates weekly offset by 1 day.
- PagerDuty schedule: primary -> secondary -> manager escalation rules as above.
- Coverage windows: Weekdays 24/7, weekends covered by same weekly rotation.
- Handoffs: Each shift handoff must occur in #oncall-incidents and include:
  1) Current active incidents and status
  2) Known degradations/ongoing mitigations
  3) Any scheduled maintenance or game days
  4) A brief summary of outstanding follow-ups and owners
- Escalation responsibilities: If primary does not ack within 5 minutes for SEV-1, PagerDuty escalates to secondary. If no ack in 30 minutes escalate to engineering manager.

Incident lifecycle procedure (step-by-step)
------------------------------------------
1) Detection
   - Alerts originate from Prometheus/Alertmanager, external monitoring, customer reports, or logs.
   - Every alert should document: alert name, threshold, time, link to dashboard, and relevant runbook.

2) Acknowledgement & Triage
   - First responder acknowledges the alert in PagerDuty and posts a short note in #oncall-incidents with incident tag and initial assessment.
   - Triage checklist:
     a) Identify impacted customers and services.
     b) Check SLO dashboards and recent deploys.
     c) Gather top 3 hypotheses and immediate mitigating actions.

3) Declare incident & create IC channel
   - If the incident meets Sev 2+ criteria, IC is appointed (usually the first responder or senior on-call).
   - Create #incident-<INCIDENT-ID> for coordination.
   - Assign roles: IC, comms lead, SME(s).

4) Mitigation and containment
   - Follow runbook(s) for the suspected failure mode (examples below).
   - Record actions and timestamps (command run, rollback, config change).

5) Communication
   - Internal: IC posts updates to #oncall-incidents every 15 minutes for SEV-1, every 30 minutes for SEV-2 until mitigated.
   - External: Comms lead posts initial status to status.redwood.ai for SEV-1 and SEV-2 within 30 minutes. Use templates provided below.

6) Resolution & recovery
   - Confirm service health via SLO dashboards and synthetic checks for a sustained 30 minutes (or per service-specific runbook).
   - Announce resolution internally and close PagerDuty incident.

7) Post-incident activities
   - IC/PM/SRE schedule a postmortem meeting within 72 hours for SEV-1, 7 days for SEV-2.
   - Postmortem must include timeline, root cause, action items, and owner for each action.

Runbook templates (examples)
---------------------------
Note: Each runbook must include Preconditions, Observable symptoms, Immediate mitigation steps, Long-term remediation, and Postmortem link.

A) API availability / control plane outage\n- Symptoms:
  - 500/502 responses spike across regions, health checks failing, traffic drop in metrics.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Verify metrics at https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/control-plane
  2) Check recent deploys: git rev, CI deploy pipeline status./deployments
  3) If deployment suspected: roll back to previous stable artifact:
     - CLI: rci deploy rollback --service control-plane --to-version <previous>
  4) If database or cache is saturated: scale read replicas or flush cache per infra runbook.
- Escalation: page DB infra team if RDS replica lag > 30s or > 1000 pending connections.

B) Serving runtime high latency / token generation slowdowns
- Symptoms:
  - p95 token latency > SLO for > 10 minutes, queue length increasing, GPU utilization abnormal.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Identify affected model(s) and pods: kubectl get pods -l service=runtime -o wide
  2) Restart affected pod(s) if memory leaks suspected: kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-model-x
  3) Temporarily route traffic to alternate model variant or lower-precision quantized variant using Routing Control Plane UI or CLI:
     - CLI: rci routing set --route <route> --model <model-quantized-v1> --weight 100
  4) Increase replica count or add burst nodes per Dedicated autoscale policy.
- Mitigation: Enable request shedding for non-critical routes and enable caching (prefix cache).

C) GPU node failure / capacity loss
- Symptoms: Node offline, pods in CrashLoopBackOff, queue backlog, scaling fails.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Verify node status: kubectl get nodes | grep -i gpu
  2) Evict affected pods: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  3) Trigger capacity burst in AWS/GCP console or via infra automation: terraform apply -var='action=burst' -target=module.gpu_pool
  4) If hardware fault suspected for on-prem: open on-call hardware ticket and follow onprem-packaging runbook.

Postmortem requirements and template
----------------------------------
Every required postmortem must include the following fields (use the postmortem template in the Postmortem repo):
- Title, incident ID, severity, date/time range, author, owners
- Timeline (5-15 minute granularity for SEV-1)
- Root cause analysis (RCA) with evidence, contributing factors, and detection gaps
- Corrective actions (short-term and long-term) with owners and due dates
- Impact summary (customers affected, SLO impact, revenue/ops impacts)
- Preventative changes (monitoring, runbook updates, automation)
- Summary and follow-up review meeting notes

Postmortem SLA
- SEV-1 initial draft: 72 hours. Finalized postmortem: 14 days.
- SEV-2 initial draft: 7 days. Finalized: 21 days.

Game days and exercises
-----------------------
- Objective: Validate runbooks, alerting, and operator coordination.
- Frequency: Quarterly service-level game days; Team-specific tabletop exercises monthly.
- Planning checklist:
  1) Define scope and objectives (what to test: e.g., routing failover, GPU pool loss).
  2) Schedule with minimal customer impact windows and notify stakeholders.
  3) Prepare test harness and rollback plan.
  4) Run exercise, capture timeline, and produce action items.
  5) Ensure at least one follow-up postmortem-style write-up and remediation plan.

Status page & customer communications templates
---------------------------------------------
Use these templates for status page posts and customer-facing emails. Customize to be concise, factual, and non-speculative.

Status page — Initial report (SEV-1/SEV-2)
Title: Service Degradation: Redwood API (Generation) — Partial Outage
Time: 2026-03-01 14:12 UTC
Summary: We are currently investigating increased errors and latency impacting text generation requests in US region. Customers may experience 500 responses or delays. Our teams are actively working on mitigation.
Impact: Some customers in the US region may see errors or latency in text generation requests.
Next update: 14:30 UTC or sooner\n
Status page — Update (Mitigation in progress)
Summary: We identified a recent model rollout as the likely cause and have routed traffic to the previous stable variant while we investigate. Error rates are decreasing but some requests still see raised latency.
Next update: 15:00 UTC\n
Status page — Resolved
Summary: The issue has been resolved. Traffic remains routed to the stable model variant while we complete post-incident verification. We will publish a postmortem with timeline and corrective actions within 72 hours.\n
Customer email template (short)
Subject: Incident update — Redwood API generation degraded (resolved)
Body: We experienced degraded text generation performance impacting some customers in the US region between 14:12 and 14:58 UTC on 2026-03-01. The team mitigated the issue by routing traffic to a stable model variant. We are investigating the root cause and will share a postmortem in 72 hours. If you have questions, contact support@redwood.ai.

Escalation decision matrix
-------------------------
| Condition | Escalate to | Timeframe |
|---|---:|---:|
| SEV-1 unacknowledged | Secondary on-call | 5 minutes |
| Repeated errors after mitigation | Engineering manager | 30 minutes |
| Data loss or PII exposure | Security lead + legal | Immediately |

Runbook maintenance and ownership
--------------------------------
- Every runbook shall have a documented owner and an assert cadence for review (quarterly). Owners are responsible for keeping runbooks executable and up to date.
- Add runbook changes as PRs to the runbook repo and tag the oncall-and-incident-response reviewers.

Metrics, dashboards and key alerts (examples)
--------------------------------------------
- API availability (SLO): 99.9% hourly for hosted-api (alert at 99.5% over 15m).
- Model-serving p95 latency: target < 600ms p95 (alert if p95 > 1200ms for 10m).
- GPU pool utilization: alert if available capacity < 20% and queue length > 1000.
- Error rate (5xx): alert if > 1% of requests or sustained 500 spikes > 30m.

Retention and compliance notes
----------------------------
- Incident artifacts (chat logs, runbook actions, PagerDuty timeline) are retained for 365 days.
- SEV categories that involve customer data or PII exposures must trigger the Security incident playbook and legal notifications.

Appendices
---------
A) Example incident timeline (abridged)
- 14:12 UTC: Monitoring alerts for 500 errors triggered
- 14:14 UTC: Primary on-call acknowledges, initial triage posted
- 14:18 UTC: IC declared; #incident-20260301-1 channel created
- 14:25 UTC: Rollback of recent model rollout started
- 14:36 UTC: Error rate falling; traffic routed to stable variant
- 14:58 UTC: Monitoring shows recovery; IC begins verification
- 15:10 UTC: Incident marked resolved; postmortem scheduled

B) Helpful links
- PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.redwood.ai/services/Redwood-Prod
- Dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template
- Runbook repo: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks\nDocument ownership

Owners: eng-sre (primary), engineering on-call rotation
